item.title: Indonesia’s Modern Pentathlon Team Wins Gold and Three More Medals at SEA Games Thailand
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s modern pentathlon team delivered a strong performance at the 2025 SEA Games in Thailand, securing one gold medal, two silvers, and one bronze to bolster the national medal tally and highlight the sport’s growing contribution to Indonesia’s competitive success. The gold medal was claimed by Dea Salsabila Putri in the women’s triathle individual event on Thursday. item.title: Migrant Workers Send Home $12.7 Billion as Indonesia Steps Up Protection
item.description: Jakarta. Remittances sent by Indonesian migrant workers reached Rp 212 trillion, or about $12.7 billion, by the end of the third quarter of 2025, highlighting their increasingly important contribution to the national economy, Migrant Worker Protection Minister Mukhtarudin said on Thursday. item.title: KPK Arrests Prosecutors and Others in Separate Raids Across Regions
item.description: Jakarta. The Corruption Eradication Commission (KPK) has reportedly detained several prosecutors and other individuals in a series of separate operations conducted over the past two days in Banten, Jakarta, and South Kalimantan. According to information obtained, KPK investigators on Thursday detained three prosecutors assigned to Hulu Sungai Utara district in South Kalimantan. item.title: Stocks Gain at Open as Global Markets Rally, Growth Risks Linger
item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index opened higher on Friday, rising 39 points or 0.45% to 8,657, supported by a positive global lead even as investors weighed a cautious medium-term outlook for Indonesia’s economy. RTI data showed trading volume reached 2.22 billion shares in the first five minutes, with turnover of Rp 1.19 trillion ($71.1 million) across more than 193,000 transactions. item.title: Antam Gold Price Dips, Ending Three-Day Uptrend
item.description: Jakarta. Antam’s gold bar price eased on Friday, retreating Rp 4,000 to Rp 2,483,000 ($148.60) per gram, pulling back from its all-time high after a sharp rally earlier this week. Data from Logam Mulia showed Antam gold had jumped Rp 17,000 on Thursday to Rp 2,487,000 per gram, marking a fresh record. item.description: As social media becomes inseparable from the daily lives of Indonesian children and teenagers, the country faces an increasingly urgent dilemma: how prepared is Indonesia to protect young people in a digital environment that evolves faster than its regulatory capacity? item.title: Sumatra Floods: Govt Says No Tax on Aid from Indonesian Diaspora
item.description: Jakarta. The government recently said that any assistance sent by Indonesian diaspora to the Sumatra flood victims would be tax-free as long as they follow the right procedures. Finance Minister Purbaya Yudhi Sadewa denied social media reports that the customs directorate general were collecting taxes on donated goods. item.title: High Costs, Not Wages, Keep Investors Away, Celios Says
item.description: Jakarta. Indonesia’s planned minimum wage increase in 2026 is unlikely to sway foreign investors, who continue to favor other Southeast Asian countries due to economic inefficiencies, an economist said Tuesday. item.description: Jakarta. The government said several global electric vehicle (EV) manufacturers plan to start producing in Indonesia from 2026 to avoid higher import duties, as incentives for fully built-up (CBU) imports expire. item.title: Tropical Cyclone Seedling 93S Puts Java, Yogyakarta on High Weather Alert
item.description: Yogyakarta. The Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysics Agency (BMKG) has warned that a developing tropical system in the Indian Ocean could trigger extreme weather across parts of the country, including Yogyakarta and large areas of Java. BMKG said it is monitoring two tropical cyclone seedlings — identified as 93S and 95S — that could affect weather and sea conditions in the coming days.
